items.title: How does granting more services PII access change expected breach exposure?
items.description: L2's classification table gates PII_RESTRICTED fields to named services only, on the logic that fewer access points means less to go wrong. Each service granted access is its own independent chance of being the one that gets compromised — a fixed per-service breach risk, applied across more services, adds up. Drag how many services are granted access and each one's yearly odds of compromise, and watch the expected number of customer records exposed per year across the whole set — not just the worst single incident.

params.name: recordsVisiblePerService
params.label: Customer records each service can query

params.name: annualBreachOddsPercent
params.label: Each service's odds of compromise per year

items.compute: const expectedRecordsExposedPerYear = params.servicesWithPiiAccess * params.recordsVisiblePerService * (params.annualBreachOddsPercent / 100); return { expectedRecordsExposedPerYear };

outputs.label: Expected records exposed per year, across all granted services

items.title: How does a longer retention window trade off against ongoing audit-log storage?
items.description: L3's audit log grows with every read and write event, forever, until a retention job clears entries past their lawful window (see enforceRetention). A longer window means more evidence available for a late-arriving audit, but also more data sitting around that has to be secured, stored, and eventually reviewed. Drag the retention window and the daily event volume to see how many events are ever resident in the log at once — the number a breach, a storage bill, or an audit response all have to contend with.
items.compute: const daysRetained = params.retentionMonths * 30; const eventsResident = params.eventsPerDay * daysRetained; return { eventsResident };

outputs.label: Audit events resident in the log at any time
